swarm.builder: hermes_cli.main kanban --board <slug> swarm (root + N workers + one verifier + one synthesizer, wired into the DAG)
swarm.goal: Execute the FAR ruling for FAR-REMEDIATION-AND-CLOSURE-20261016: rebind the PLAN route row to the owner-ordered arm (R1), reclassify the declared SoD conflict (R3), promote the verified candidate product files with the oracle orchestrator-side (R2), implement the additive dispatcher turn-shape flag via the EXECUTE lane in an edit-only turn (R5), then independently verify, close and publish
worker_titles: R1-R3 registry ruling applied under WorkOrder
R2 promotion of the verified candidate product set

what_kanban_swarm_openspec_are_not: They are ORCHESTRATION surfaces (task graph, change record, board), NOT model routers: creating them routes no model and selects no arm.

Which model serves which role is fixed by the lane binding (the governed profile for the in-Hermes PLAN plane; scripts/hgk-lane-dispatch.py --require-arm --force-rank for the CODEX CLI lanes), independently of these surfaces.
GSTACK has no separate implementation in this repository; it is reported as a named-method / role-map readback, never as an enabled component.
dispatch_note: Cards are recorded graph evidence. The arms this round actually consumes are proven by the CODEX CLI dispatch receipts (required_arm == served_arm) and by the governed profile's own session rows, not by these card ids.
claim_ceiling: A card id is not a run. This artifact records the graph and its builders; it asserts nothing about the model that served any turn.
